# Marginalia

The first correction appeared in October, in a copy of *The Old Man and the Sea* that had circulated through the Kettle Harbor Public Library forty-three times. Marisol Reyes found it while checking the book back in: a pencilled note in the margin beside Hemingway's description of the Gulf Stream, written in a small, careful hand.

*The current runs closer to shore in September. He would have known that.*

Marisol frowned. She was supposed to flag any defacement—dog-ears, coffee rings, highlighter—and pull the book for repair or replacement. Instead, she found herself holding the page under the desk lamp, tilting it. The pencil marks were so light they nearly disappeared at an angle. Whoever had written them had tried, somehow, to be respectful of the book even while arguing with it.

She should have erased it. She got as far as pulling out the pink eraser from the drawer of odds and ends. Then she put it back.
